q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
explain: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
hook: Jupiter, king of the Roman gods, is king of the planets.

sources.title: Planet Sizes and Locations in Our Solar System - NASA Science
sources.quote: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system. It’s about 11 times wider than Earth with an equatorial diameter of 88,846 miles (about 142,984 kilometers).

sources.title: About the Planets - NASA Science
sources.quote: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun, and the largest planet in our solar system.

q: Which planet is nearest to the Sun?
explain: Mercury is the planet nearest to the Sun, and also the smallest planet in our solar system.
hook: Mercury, the messenger god, stays closest to the Sun.

sources.title: Mercury: Facts - NASA Science
sources.quote: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun.

sources.title: About the Planets - NASA Science
sources.quote: Mercury is the planet nearest to the Sun, and the smallest planet in our solar system.

q: On which planet is Olympus Mons, the largest known volcano in the solar system?
explain: Olympus Mons, on Mars, is the largest known volcano in the solar system.
hook: Olympus for the gods, Olympus Mons for Mars.

sources.title: Mars: Facts - NASA Science
sources.quote: Mars is home to the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons .

sources.title: Olympus Mons | Description, Height, & Facts | Britannica
sources.quote: Olympus Mons , volcano on the planet Mars , the highest point on the planet and the largest known volcano in the solar system .

q: Which planet rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle to its orbit, so it appears to spin on its side?
explain: Uranus rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle from the plane of its orbit, so it appears to spin on its side.
hook: Uranus rolls around the Sun like a ball.

sources.title: Uranus: Facts - NASA Science
sources.quote: Uranus rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle from the plane of its orbit. This unique tilt makes Uranus appear to spin sideways, orbiting the Sun like a rolling ball.

sources.title: Uranus - NASA Science
sources.quote: It rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle from the plane of its orbit. This unique tilt makes Uranus appear to spin on its side.

q: Which Apollo 11 astronaut stayed in lunar orbit while Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon?
explain: The Apollo 11 crew was Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin; Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the lunar surface while Collins remained in orbit around the Moon.

sources.title: What Was the Apollo Program? - NASA
sources.quote: The crew of Apollo 11 was Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin. Armstong and Aldrin walked on the lunar surface while Collins remained in orbit around the moon.

sources.title: A Brief History of the Apollo Program | Smithsonian Institution
sources.quote: Michael Collins piloted the CSM Columbia mothership.

q: How many astronauts have walked on the Moon?
explain: A total of 12 astronauts walked on the Moon, all of them during the Apollo program.

sources.title: What Was the Apollo Program? - NASA
sources.quote: A total of 12 astronauts walked on the moon.

sources.title: How Many People Have Been to the Moon? | Britannica
sources.quote: In fact, during nine Apollo missions, 24 astronauts (all Americans) went to the Moon, and 12 of them walked on it.

q: Approximately how long is one astronomical unit (AU), the average Earth-Sun distance?
explain: One AU, the average distance between Earth and the Sun, is about 150 million km (about 93 million miles).

sources.title: Astronomical unit (AU, or au) | Britannica
sources.quote: An astronomical unit (AU) is a unit of length equal to the average distance between Earth and the Sun, which is about 149.6 million kilometers (92.96 million miles).

sources.title: Cosmic Distances - NASA Science
sources.quote: One AU is the distance from the Sun to Earth's orbit, which is about 93 million miles (150 million kilometers).

q: Which star is the nearest to the Sun?
explain: Proxima Centauri, the dimmest of the three stars in the Alpha Centauri system, is the nearest star to the Sun.

sources.title: The Nearest Neighbor Star - Imagine the Universe! - NASA
sources.quote: Of the three stars in the system, the dimmest - called Proxima Centauri - is actually the nearest star to the Sun.

sources.title: Sun: Facts - NASA Science
sources.quote: Its nearest stellar neighbor is the Alpha Centauri triple star system: red dwarf star Proxima Centauri is 4.24 light-years away, and Alpha Centauri A and B – two sunlike stars orbiting each other – are 4.37 light-years away.

q: Nuclear fusion in the Sun's core converts hydrogen into which element?
explain: In the Sun's core, nuclear reactions fuse hydrogen to form helium, releasing the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light.

sources.title: NASA/Marshall Solar Physics
sources.quote: The Sun's core is the central region where nuclear reactions consume hydrogen to form helium. These reactions release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light.

sources.title: Chapter 1: The Solar System - NASA Science
sources.quote: The Sun's gravity creates extreme pressures and temperatures within its core, sustaining a thermonuclear reaction fusing hydrogen nuclei and producing helium nuclei.

q: What is the name of the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way?
explain: Sagittarius A* (Sgr A* for short) is the supermassive black hole at the centre of our Milky Way galaxy; the Event Horizon Telescope produced the first image of it.

sources.title: Astronomers Reveal First Image of the Black Hole at the Heart of Our Galaxy | Event Horizon Telescope
sources.quote: This is the first image of Sagittarius A* (or Sgr A* for short), the supermassive black hole at the centre of our galaxy.

sources.title: Black Hole Image Makes History; NASA Telescopes Coordinated Observations - NASA
sources.quote: also looked at the black hole at the center of our own Milky Way galaxy, called Sagittarius A*, in coordination with EHT.

q: What is the nearest large galaxy to our Milky Way?
explain: The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) is a spiral galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away and one of the few galaxies visible to the unaided eye.

sources.title: Andromeda Galaxy | Description, Location, Distance, & Facts | Britannica
sources.quote: Andromeda Galaxy , (catalog numbers NGC 224 and M31), great spiral galaxy in the constellation Andromeda , the nearest large galaxy. The Andromeda Galaxy is one of the few visible to the unaided eye, appearing as a milky blur. It is located about 2,480,000 light-years from Earth

sources.title: Messier 31 (The Andromeda Galaxy) - NASA Science
sources.quote: M31, also well-known as the Andromeda Galaxy, is the nearest major galaxy to our own, the Milky Way.

q: On what date was the James Webb Space Telescope launched?
explain: Webb launched on December 25, 2021, aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana.

sources.title: Webb's Launch - NASA Science
sources.quote: Webb was launched on on December 25, 2021 on board an Ariane 5 rocket from Ariane Space Spaceport in French Guiana.

sources.title: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) | Britannica
sources.quote: launched by an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou , French Guiana , on December 25, 2021. The JWST has a mirror 6.5 metres (21.3 feet) in diameter, seven times larger than that of the HST, and orbits the Sun in a Lissajous pattern around the second Lagrangian point , about 1.5 million km (930,000 miles) from Earth

q: Which spacecraft became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space, in August 2012?
explain: Voyager 1 reached interstellar space in August 2012, becoming the first human-made object to do so.

sources.title: Interstellar Mission - NASA Science
sources.quote: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space on Aug. 25, 2012, becoming the first human-made object to do so.

sources.title: NASA Spacecraft Embarks on Historic Journey into Interstellar Space - NASA
sources.quote: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft officially is the first human-made object to venture into interstellar space.

sources.title: Voyager 1 - NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
sources.quote: Voyager 1 reached interstellar space in August 2012 and is the most distant human-made object in existence.

q: What is the name of the gold-plated copper disk of sounds and images from Earth carried by both Voyager spacecraft?
explain: Both Voyager spacecraft carry the Golden Record, a 12-inch gold-plated copper disk containing sounds and images selected to portray life and culture on Earth.

sources.title: Voyager 1 - NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
sources.quote: Both spacecraft carry a sort of time capsule called the Golden Record, a 12-inch gold-plated copper disk containing sounds and images selected to portray the story of our world to extraterrestrials.

sources.title: Golden Record Overview - NASA Science
sources.quote: The Voyager message is carried by a phonograph record, a 12-inch gold-plated copper disk containing sounds and images selected to portray the diversity of life and culture on Earth.
